Reviewer QUAL:
Reviewer dimension: QUAL
Paper summary: The paper proposes a multimodal variational NMT model that introduces a continuous latent variable z aimed at capturing sentence-level semantics by combining text and image information during training. The posterior q(z|x,y,π) conditions on source, target, and image; the prior p(z|x) depends only on the source to enable test-time translation without images. The latent variable is integrated into a conditional GRU decoder. The authors evaluate on Multi30k (EN–DE), compare to text-only NMT with attention and VNMT, explore several image-encoding strategies, and report improvements in METEOR and BLEU over baselines.

Dimension score (1-10): 6
Confidence (1-5): 3

Sub-dimension scores:
- QUAL-MET: 7/10
- QUAL-EXP: 5/10
- QUAL-REP: 7/10
- QUAL-CMP: 4/10
- QUAL-STA: 3/10

Strengths:
- Sound variational formulation with a clear separation between training posterior and test-time prior; end-to-end differentiable objective with reparameterization and closed-form KL for Gaussians (Eq. 2), consistent with VAE practice (SRC-028(page=2); SRC-031(page=3); SRC-061(page=5); SRC-062(page=5)).
- Practical multimodal design that leverages images only during training via q(z|x,y,π) and p(z|x) for testing, addressing realistic settings where images are unavailable at inference (SRC-031(page=3); SRC-058(page=5)).
- Multiple image-encoding variants and qualitative/quantitative analyses provide some ablations and insights (SRC-037(page=3), SRC-038(page=3), SRC-039(page=3), SRC-040(page=3), SRC-041(page=3), SRC-042(page=4), SRC-043(page=4), SRC-044(page=4); SRC-074(page=6); SRC-076(page=6)).
- Reasonable experimental setup on a standard multimodal dataset (Multi30k), with established metrics (METEOR, BLEU), and typical training details (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-070(page=6); SRC-066(page=5), SRC-067(page=5), SRC-068(page=5), SRC-069(page=5)).

Weaknesses:
- Limited comparative evaluation: unclear or incomplete comparisons to strong multimodal baselines (e.g., the CMU approach), and reliance on a single dataset of modest size (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-071(page=6); SRC-072(page=6)).
- Lack of statistical rigor: no significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; acknowledged unexplained training instabilities and overfitting (SRC-075(page=6); SRC-077(page=6)).
- Some ambiguity in key implementation specifics in the main text (integration details deferred to the appendix; hyperparameters said to be in the appendix but not fully visible here), and no code release mentioned (SRC-059(page=5); SRC-068(page=5)).
- Methodological risks like posterior collapse or balancing the KL term are not discussed, and there is no analysis of the latent variable’s utilization.

Detailed assessment by sub-dimension:
- QUAL-MET: strength: The probabilistic model is well-specified: ELBO with posterior q(z|x,y,π) and prior p(z|x) is standard and appropriate for training-time multimodal information with test-time text-only translation (Eq. 2). Reparameterization, Monte Carlo (L=1), and analytical KL for Gaussians are appropriate and differentiable (SRC-028(page=2); SRC-031(page=3); SRC-061(page=5); SRC-062(page=5)). Integrating z into a conditional GRU decoder aligns with prior VNMT formulations, and the architecture decomposition (encoder/inferrer/decoder) is coherent (SRC-032(page=3); SRC-058(page=5); SRC-059(page=5)). weakness: The paper does not discuss potential issues such as posterior collapse or mechanisms (e.g., KL annealing, word dropout) to ensure the model uses z; important decoder integration specifics are relegated to the appendix (SRC-059(page=5)).
- QUAL-EXP: strength: Uses Multi30k with clear train/val/test splits and standard preprocessing; evaluates with METEOR and BLEU; explores multiple image-encoding strategies and provides quantitative/qualitative analysis, including length-based effects (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-066(page=5); SRC-067(page=5); SRC-070(page=6); SRC-037(page=3), SRC-038(page=3), SRC-039(page=3), SRC-040(page=3), SRC-041(page=3), SRC-042(page=4), SRC-043(page=4), SRC-044(page=4); SRC-072(page=6); SRC-076(page=6)). weakness: The evaluation is limited to a single dataset; the baselines include NMT and VNMT but comparisons against the strongest WMT16 multimodal systems are unclear in terms of numbers; no ablations on the contribution of the prior vs. posterior or analysis of test-time behavior beyond a single design; unexplained validation jumps and overfitting suggest instability (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-072(page=6); SRC-075(page=6); SRC-077(page=6)).
- QUAL-REP: strength: Provides substantial implementation details: feature extractors (VGG-19 fc7, Fast R-CNN), preprocessing steps (Moses scripts, BPE-like compound splitting), optimizer (Adadelta), initialization, beam size, early stopping, and implementation base (dl4mt), and notes about decoder differences (conditional GRU) (SRC-066(page=5); SRC-067(page=5); SRC-068(page=5); SRC-069(page=5); SRC-070(page=6)). weakness: The main text relies on the appendix for hyperparameters; code availability is not stated; exact data splits and random seeds for reproducibility and variance estimation are missing (SRC-068(page=5); SRC-070(page=6)).
- QUAL-CMP: strength: Related work is reasonably surveyed, including contemporaneous multimodal NMT approaches and VNMT, with motivation about difficulty of integrating images and text (SRC-020(page=2); SRC-021(page=2); SRC-022(page=2); SRC-023(page=2); SRC-027(page=2)). weakness: Empirical comparisons to strong recent multimodal NMT systems (e.g., CMU) are not clearly presented in results; claims of outperforming the baseline do not establish state-of-the-art standing (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-072(page=6)).
- QUAL-STA: strength: None substantial beyond reporting standard metrics. weakness: No significance tests, confidence intervals, or multiple seeds; acknowledged fluctuations and unexpected validation spikes without analysis; dataset overfitting mentioned but not mitigated or quantified statistically (SRC-072(page=6); SRC-075(page=6); SRC-077(page=6)).

Evidence anchors used:
- SRC-028(page=2): Introduces the ELBO for the proposed model, supporting methodological soundness in variational formulation.
- SRC-031(page=3): Clarifies the use of p(z|x) for test-time decoding without images, supporting the practicality of the approach.
- SRC-061(page=5): Describes Monte Carlo estimation with L=1 for the ELBO expectation, indicating standard VAE training practice.
- SRC-062(page=5): Notes closed-form KL for Gaussians and differentiability, reinforcing soundness of optimization.
- SRC-058(page=5): Defines the decoder probability p(y|z,x), aligning with VNMT-like architectures.

- SRC-065(page=5): Provides dataset and splits, supporting experimental setup adequacy.

- SRC-067(page=5): Specifies image feature extraction (VGG-19 fc7; Fast R-CNN), relevant for reproduction.
- SRC-068(page=5): Gives optimization details (init, Adadelta, early stopping, beam), aiding reproducibility.
- SRC-069(page=5) and SRC-070(page=6): Implementation base (dl4mt) and metric use (METEOR, BLEU), enabling comparison.
- SRC-037(page=3), SRC-038(page=3), SRC-039(page=3), SRC-040(page=3), SRC-041(page=3), SRC-042(page=4), SRC-043(page=4), SRC-044(page=4): Describes multiple image encoding variants, forming experimental ablations.
- SRC-072(page=6): Claims that models outperform baseline and references figures, grounding the main result.
- SRC-074(page=6): Provides analysis that “G” variant performs best and discusses challenges with object-based features.
- SRC-075(page=6): Mentions unexplained validation behavior and stability observations, revealing instability.
- SRC-077(page=6): Notes overfitting on Multi30k and possible dataset limitations, highlighting statistical concerns.
- SRC-022(page=2): References CMU’s strong WMT16 multimodal NMT model and the intent to compare, indicating needed baseline.

Key questions for the authors:
- Please report statistical significance (e.g., paired bootstrap or approximate randomization) and variance across multiple random seeds for METEOR and BLEU to validate that gains over VNMT and NMT are robust (related to SRC-072(page=6), SRC-075(page=6)).
- Can you provide quantitative comparisons to the strongest WMT16 multimodal NMT systems (e.g., CMU) under the same preprocessing and data splits to situate your method against prior multimodal SOTA (SRC-022(page=2))?
- What measures did you take to prevent posterior collapse? Did you monitor KL term usage or apply techniques like KL annealing or word dropout? Please include analyses showing that the decoder effectively uses z.
- Please include the full hyperparameter settings from the appendix in the main supplementary material and release code/checkpoints to enhance reproducibility (SRC-068(page=5), SRC-069(page=5), SRC-070(page=6)).
- Can you clarify the exact integration of z into the conditional GRU (now in the appendix) in the main text and provide an ablation isolating the contribution of image-conditioned q(z|x,y,π) vs. text-only q(z|x,y)?

Recommendation: Weak Reject

Reviewer SIGN:
Reviewer dimension: SIGN
Paper summary: The paper proposes a multimodal variational NMT model that introduces a continuous latent variable z capturing underlying semantics inferred jointly from source text, target text, and images during training, while relying only on the source text at test time via a learned prior p(z|x). The model extends Variational NMT (VNMT) by adding image information into the posterior q(z|x,y,π) and concatenating text and image encodings in the encoder, with several image-encoding strategies considered. Experiments on the Multi30k English–German dataset report that the proposed model outperforms baselines in METEOR and BLEU, with larger gains on shorter sentences.

Dimension score (1-10): 6
Confidence (1-5): 3

Sub-dimension scores:
- SIGN-BRD: 6/10
- SIGN-DOM: 6/10
- SIGN-SOT: 5/10
- SIGN-IMP: 3/10

Strengths:
- Introduces a principled multimodal variational formulation that uses images only to shape the latent semantics during training, maintaining test-time practicality by conditioning the prior on source text only (p(z|x)) (SRC-031(page=3); SRC-046(page=4)).
- Provides evidence of consistent improvements over baselines on Multi30k in both METEOR and BLEU, with especially notable gains on short sentences, suggesting the latent multimodal signal helps disambiguation (SRC-072(page=6); SRC-076(page=6)).
- Situates the work within the multimodal MT literature and addresses a known challenge—leveraging images without hurting text-only performance—by projecting text and images into a common semantic latent space (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-023(page=2); SRC-027(page=2)).

Weaknesses:
- The empirical scope is limited to a single, relatively small captioning dataset (Multi30k), which has known risks of overfitting and may not reflect broader translation scenarios (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-077(page=6)).
- Reported improvements are not quantified in detail here, and there is no clear comparison against the strongest multimodal baselines (e.g., the CMU approach highlighted in WMT16) to establish state-of-the-art advances (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-072(page=6)).
- The paper does not discuss societal impacts, fairness, or environmental considerations of multimodal training, nor who benefits or may be harmed, limiting the assessment of practical and societal significance.

Detailed assessment by sub-dimension:
- SIGN-BRD: strength: The work tackles a broadly relevant problem—integrating perceptual and linguistic signals for machine translation—by introducing a latent semantic space that may inform other multimodal generation tasks beyond MT. The architectural choice to learn p(z|x) enables deployment without images, increasing broader applicability (SRC-027(page=2); SRC-031(page=3); SRC-046(page=4)). weakness: Breadth is constrained by evaluation on a narrow domain and dataset; the paper itself notes overfitting tendencies on Multi30k, reducing confidence in generalizable insights (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-077(page=6)). evidence: SRC-027(page=2), SRC-031(page=3), SRC-046(page=4), SRC-065(page=5), SRC-077(page=6).
- SIGN-DOM: strength: Within multimodal MT, the method shows improvement in standard metrics and offers analysis that image-guided latent variables help more on shorter sentences—actionable knowledge for practitioners working on caption-like data (SRC-072(page=6); SRC-076(page=6)). weakness: The domain significance is weakened by a lack of thorough comparisons to leading multimodal systems from WMT16 and by reliance on a single dataset with limited linguistic variety (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-065(page=5)). evidence: SRC-072(page=6), SRC-076(page=6), SRC-022(page=2), SRC-065(page=5).
- SIGN-SOT: strength: The paper claims improvements over VNMT/NMT baselines in METEOR and BLEU, indicating potential methodological value, and ties the gains to a clear mechanism (multimodal q and text-only p) (SRC-072(page=6); SRC-046(page=4)). weakness: The magnitude and consistency of gains are not detailed here, statistical significance is not discussed, and there is no head-to-head with the strongest multimodal SOTA, limiting the case for a state-of-the-art advance (SRC-022(page=2); SRC-072(page=6)). evidence: SRC-072(page=6), SRC-046(page=4), SRC-022(page=2).
- SIGN-IMP: strength: Practicality is considered by avoiding image dependence at inference via p(z|x), which can reduce deployment friction (SRC-031(page=3); SRC-046(page=4)). weakness: There is no discussion of real-world societal impacts (benefits/harms), bias/fairness issues in multimodal data, or environmental costs of multimodal training, limiting the work’s articulated societal significance. evidence: SRC-031(page=3), SRC-046(page=4).

Evidence anchors used:
- SRC-027(page=2): Introduces a latent variable capturing semantics from both text and image—core to the claimed contribution.
- SRC-031(page=3): Models p(z|x) to enable translation from source alone at test time—key to practicality and broader impact.
- SRC-046(page=4): Specifies modeling both q(z|x,y,π) and p(z|x), reinforcing the “images only in training” setup.
- SRC-072(page=6): States that proposed models outperform baselines in METEOR and BLEU, supporting claimed improvements.
- SRC-076(page=6): Shows larger gains on short sentences, contributing to domain-specific insights.
- SRC-022(page=2): Contextualizes prior multimodal NMT attempts and their challenges, framing the significance.
- SRC-065(page=5): Details the dataset (Multi30k) and its size, grounding concerns about generalizability.
- SRC-077(page=6): Notes overfitting issues in Multi30k, tempering impact claims.

Key questions for the authors:
- What are the exact METEOR and BLEU gains over NMT and VNMT, with variance or statistical significance? Can you provide per-length breakdowns and ablations quantifying the contribution of image-conditioned q versus text-only p?
- How does the proposed method compare against the strongest multimodal baselines (e.g., the WMT16 CMU approach) under identical settings?
- Can you demonstrate generalization beyond Multi30k, e.g., on other multimodal translation benchmarks or text-only MT tasks to validate the learned latent priors?
- What are the societal implications of using image data during training (e.g., potential bias amplification from visual datasets)? Any considerations for environmental cost or fairness and how to mitigate them?

Recommendation: Borderline
Reviewer ORIG:
Reviewer dimension: ORIG
Paper summary: The paper extends Variational Neural Machine Translation (VNMT) by introducing a continuous latent variable z that captures underlying semantics from both text and images during training, while relying only on source text at test time via a learned prior p(z|x). The model uses a VAE-style posterior q(z|x,y,π) incorporating image features and explores several image encoding strategies (global features, object-based averages, RNN over object features, and injecting image features as pseudo-tokens). Experiments on Multi30k show modest improvements over baselines (NMT and VNMT) in BLEU/METEOR, with observations that gains are larger for short sentences, that global image features work better than object-based variants, and that the dataset is prone to overfitting.

Dimension score (1-10): 7
Confidence (1-5): 3

Sub-dimension scores:
- ORIG-PROB: 7/10
- ORIG-MTH: 6/10
- ORIG-ANL: 5/10
- ORIG-EXP: 5/10
- ORIG-COM: 7/10
- ORIG-NEG: 6/10

Strengths:
- Clear articulation of a training-test regime where images are used only during training, enabled by learning a prior p(z|x) for test-time translation; this setting is practically motivated and distinct from most contemporaneous multimodal MT that requires images at test time (SRC-031(page=3)).
- Conceptual contribution of projecting text and images into a common latent semantic space via a VAE, addressing the modality gap more systematically than simply concatenating image features in NMT (SRC-023(page=2); SRC-027(page=2)).
- Creative combination of VNMT with multimodal inputs in the posterior and a source-only prior, to exploit images without test-time dependence (SRC-028(page=2); SRC-031(page=3)).
- Exploration of multiple image encoding strategies (global, objects-avg, objects-RNN, and injecting into text), which, while incremental, broadens understanding of multimodal cues in this latent-variable framework (SRC-039(page=3), SRC-040(page=3), SRC-041(page=3), SRC-042(page=4), SRC-043(page=4), SRC-044(page=4)).
- Reporting and discussing negative/neutral findings (e.g., object features and R-CNN variants underperform), providing insights about why some multimodal designs may fail (SRC-074(page=6)).

Weaknesses:
- The methodological novelty is largely an incremental extension of VNMT by adding image features to the VAE posterior and adjusting the prior; it does not introduce a fundamentally new learning principle (SRC-027(page=2); SRC-031(page=3)).
- Analysis and insights are mostly empirical and surface-level; there is limited principled or theoretical analysis of why certain image encodings work or fail beyond plausible conjectures (SRC-074(page=6), SRC-075(page=6), SRC-076(page=6)).
- No new dataset, benchmark, or evaluation protocol is introduced; experiments rely on Multi30k and standard metrics (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-070(page=6)).
- The claim of being “the first” to use images only in training for MT is suggested but not rigorously positioned against all prior multimodal MT work; a more comprehensive related-work contrast would strengthen the originality claim (SRC-027(page=2); SRC-031(page=3)).

Detailed assessment by sub-dimension:
- ORIG-PROB: strength: The work explicitly defines and motivates a multimodal training-only setting where images are used to inform a latent z during training but are not required at test time, aligning with real-world constraints and differing from standard multimodal MT tasks (SRC-031(page=3)). weakness: The problem setup is not formalized as a benchmark task or protocol and lacks broader positioning versus existing multimodal shared tasks beyond brief mentions (SRC-020(page=2), SRC-021(page=2), SRC-022(page=2), SRC-023(page=2)). evidence: SRC-031(page=3) states modeling p(z|x) “so that we can generate a translation from the source in testing,” and Figure 1 caption indicates image inputs used only during training.

- ORIG-MTH: strength: The introduction of a VAE posterior q(z|x,y,π) that fuses text and image features, coupled with a source-only prior p(z|x) for test-time inference, is a coherent architectural extension of VNMT to absorb cross-modal information (SRC-028(page=2), SRC-029(page=2), SRC-030(page=3), SRC-031(page=3), SRC-032(page=3)). weakness: Beyond integrating image features into the VAE posterior and experimenting with straightforward image encoders, the core algorithmic contribution is incremental relative to VNMT (SRC-027(page=2)). evidence: SRC-027(page=2) frames the model as an “extension of VNMT by adding image information,” and SRC-028(page=2), SRC-029(page=2), SRC-030(page=3), SRC-031(page=3), SRC-032(page=3) detail the lower bound and neural instantiations.

- ORIG-ANL: strength: The paper offers empirical insights: global image features outperform object-based strategies and gains are larger on short sentences; it also notes increased stability with image information (SRC-074(page=6), SRC-075(page=6), SRC-076(page=6)). weakness: The analysis is largely observational without deeper diagnostic experiments or theoretical backing to explain modality interactions or latent variable behavior (SRC-075(page=6), SRC-076(page=6), SRC-077(page=6) acknowledging unexplained behavior and overfitting). evidence: SRC-074(page=6) and SRC-076(page=6) discuss performance patterns and likely causes.

- ORIG-EXP: strength: The exploration of several image encoding pipelines within the same framework adds experimental variety and informs design choices (SRC-039(page=3), SRC-040(page=3), SRC-041(page=3), SRC-042(page=4), SRC-043(page=4), SRC-044(page=4)). weakness: No new datasets or evaluation protocols are proposed; the setup is based on a single dataset (Multi30k) and standard metrics (SRC-065(page=5); SRC-070(page=6)). evidence: SRC-065(page=5) and SRC-070(page=6) document the dataset and metrics.

- ORIG-COM: strength: The paper compellingly combines VNMT’s latent semantic modeling with multimodal image-text fusion in the posterior while maintaining source-only operation at test time via the prior, addressing the modality gap critique of prior work that simply concatenated features (SRC-023(page=2); SRC-031(page=3)). weakness: Some of the specific combinations (e.g., injecting image vectors as tokens) mirror prior multimodal techniques and contribute less novelty (SRC-043(page=4)). evidence: SRC-023(page=2) motivates the common latent space approach; SRC-043(page=4) describes the G+O-TXT variant.

- ORIG-NEG: strength: The authors candidly report that object-based encodings and R-CNN features did not help and hypothesize reasons, contributing useful negative findings for the community (SRC-074(page=6)). weakness: The negative results are not deeply dissected with ablations isolating factors (e.g., number of objects, feature layer choice), limiting the depth of the critical assessment (SRC-074(page=6)). evidence: SRC-074(page=6) explicitly states proposed models do not benefit from R-CNN and discusses potential confusion from averaging multiple image features.

Key questions for the authors:
- Can you more explicitly contrast your “images used only at training time” setting with prior multimodal MT tasks and provide references to clarify whether this is indeed the first such setup in MT? Any related work in semi-supervised or weakly supervised multimodal learning that you can discuss?
- What happens if the prior p(z|x) is conditioned on additional inductive biases (e.g., image-tag predictions) at test time? Would this further reduce the train-test modality gap?
- Can you provide deeper analyses of why object-based encodings underperform (e.g., varying the number of detected objects, different CNN layers, attention over object features within q(z|·)) to turn negative findings into more generalizable insights?

Recommendation: Weak Accept

Experiments on English–German show modest improvements over baselines on METEOR and BLEU.

Recommendation: Weak Reject
Final Meta-Reviewer:
Final summary: This paper extends Variational Neural Machine Translation (VNMT) by introducing a continuous latent variable inferred from both text and images during training via a VAE, while relying only on a source-conditioned prior at test time. The authors explore several image-encoding strategies, train end-to-end on Multi30k, and report improvements over NMT and VNMT in METEOR and BLEU, with larger gains on short sentences. Conceptually, the “images only in training” setup is practical and well-motivated. However, the work suffers from limited empirical scope, missing or deferred technical details, lack of statistical rigor, and some policy/compliance gaps around human evaluation and data licensing.

Consensus strengths:
- Principled variational formulation that separates a multimodal training posterior q(z|x,y,π) from a text-only test-time prior p(z|x), enabling deployment without images.
- End-to-end differentiable training with standard VAE machinery and conditional-GRU-based decoding; clear high-level architecture decomposition (encoder/inferrer/decoder).
- Practical problem setting: using images only during training aligns with realistic MT scenarios lacking images at inference.
- Exploration of multiple image-encoding strategies with quantitative and qualitative analyses, including insights that global features work better than object-based encodings and that gains concentrate on short sentences.
- Reasonable experimental setup on a standard dataset with established metrics and baseline comparisons to NMT and VNMT.

Consensus weaknesses:
- Limited evaluation: single small dataset (Multi30k), no tests beyond caption-like text, and absent head-to-head comparisons with strongest contemporaneous multimodal baselines (e.g., WMT16 CMU).
- Statistical rigor is lacking: no significance tests, no multi-seed variance, and acknowledged training instabilities/overfitting without mitigation or analysis.
- Clarity and completeness issues: several key equations and integration details (e.g., μ/σ mappings, decoder integration) are missing from the main text or deferred to an appendix; notation inconsistencies and figure/caption shortcomings.
- Methodological risks such as posterior collapse and how z is actually utilized are not analyzed; there is no evidence the latent variable meaningfully contributes beyond standard attention.
- Policy/compliance gaps: human evaluation with native speakers is mentioned without IRB/consent details; no discussion of dataset/model licensing or broader impact, bias, or privacy considerations.

Cross-review synthesis:
- QUAL: Assesses the probabilistic formulation as sound and practically motivated but flags limited comparative evaluation, lack of statistical rigor, missing implementation specifics in the main text, and absent analysis of latent variable usage or collapse. Recommends Weak Reject.
- CLAR: Finds the high-level structure clear but identifies many missing or incomplete mathematical/algorithmic details, notation errors, and reliance on an appendix, along with figure/caption issues. Recommends Weak Reject.
- SIGN: Recognizes the practical significance of images-only-in-training and consistent gains on Multi30k, but notes the restricted empirical scope and lack of SOTA comparisons. Rates significance as moderate and recommends Borderline.
- ORIG: Sees the training-only multimodal framing and VAE-based fusion as a meaningful, if incremental, extension of VNMT, with useful negative findings on object-based encodings. Recommends Weak Accept based on conceptual novelty and practical framing, while acknowledging limited depth of analysis and scope.
- POL: Flags absence of ethics/impact discussion, missing IRB/consent details for human evaluation, and no clarity on data/software licensing or privacy safeguards, along with no broader impact considerations. Recommends Weak Reject.

Actionable suggestions:
- Strengthen empirical evidence: report results over multiple random seeds with confidence intervals or significance tests (e.g., paired bootstrap) for METEOR and BLEU; provide per-length and per-category breakdowns to substantiate claims about short sentences.
- Add comparisons to strong multimodal baselines under identical preprocessing and splits (e.g., WMT16 CMU model), and consider additional datasets or text-only tasks to test whether learned priors generalize beyond caption-style data.
- Complete the technical presentation: include explicit equations for posterior/prior parameterizations (μ and log σ^2 mappings), the full ELBO optimized in practice, and concise in-text equations showing how z is integrated into the conditional GRU. Fix notation errors (e.g., forward/backward RNN arrows) and ensure all cross-references (e.g., context vectors, Eq. 15) are defined.
- Analyze latent variable utilization: monitor KL terms during training; consider KL annealing, word dropout, or other techniques to avoid posterior collapse; add ablations isolating the contribution of image-conditioned q(z|x,y,π) versus text-only q(z|x,y) to quantify the benefit of images.
- Improve clarity and accessibility: revise writing for grammar and consistency; expand figure captions; avoid reliance on color-only references; ensure all referenced figures/tables are present and fully labeled.
- Enhance reproducibility: provide full hyperparameters and training schedules in the main or supplementary material; release code, pretrained models, and scripts (with licenses) to facilitate replication.
- Address policy/ethics: add a broader impact/ethics statement discussing potential biases in multimodal data, privacy concerns, and dual-use risks; describe IRB/ethics approval and informed consent procedures for the human evaluation; clarify dataset and software licensing and how usage complies with terms; suggest safeguards if applied to images with identifiable individuals.
